lessons.title: Add and subtract with numerical denominators
lessons.summary: Find a common denominator, scale whole numerators and subtract brackets in Extended algebraic fractions.
lessons.objective: Find a common denominator, scale whole numerators and subtract brackets in Extended algebraic fractions.
lessons.before: For 0580 Extended. Recall how to multiply, divide, add and subtract ordinary fractions. Use brackets to keep a whole numerator or denominator together.
lessons.ideas:
The fractions count equal-sized parts when their denominators match. Combine their numerators and keep the denominator once.

Use a common multiple of the bottom numbers. The lowest common multiple usually makes the arithmetic shorter.

Put the complete second numerator in brackets. The minus sign applies to every term inside those brackets.
lessons.method:
What if the denominators are already the same?

The same rule works with algebra in the numerator. \(\frac{5x}{9}+\frac{2x}{9}=\frac{7x}{9}\) because both terms count ninths.

How do I find a useful common denominator?

For denominators \(6\) and \(15\), use \(30\). Multiply the first numerator by 5 and the second by 2. Scale the whole numerator each time.

What does a minus sign subtract?

Write an expression without a denominator over \(1\). When changing its denominator, multiply each term of that expression.
mistakes: Keep the common denominator underneath the whole new numerator.
Changing only the bottom changes the fraction. Multiply both its top and its bottom by the same factor.
If the numerator already contains a minus, subtracting that negative term makes it positive. Open brackets before collecting terms.

examples.title: Use a common numerical denominator
examples.question: Write \(\frac{3 x + 9}{6}+\frac{3 x - 17}{6}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution:
A common denominator is \(6\). Multiply the first numerator by 1 and the second by 1.

The combined fraction is \(\frac{1\left(3 x + 9\right)+1\left(3 x - 17\right)}{6}\). Open the brackets, collect terms and reduce any common factor.

The simplified result is \(\frac{3 x - 4}{3}\).

examples.title: Use a common numerical denominator
examples.question: Write \(\frac{7 x + 7}{8}+\frac{4 x - 5}{12}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution:
A common denominator is \(24\). Multiply the first numerator by 3 and the second by 2.

The combined fraction is \(\frac{3\left(7 x + 7\right)+2\left(4 x - 5\right)}{24}\). Open the brackets, collect terms and reduce any common factor.

The simplified result is \(\frac{29 x + 11}{24}\).

examples.title: Subtract the whole numerator
examples.question: Write \(\frac{4 x + 5}{6}-\frac{5 x - 10}{10}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution:
A common denominator is \(30\). Multiply the first numerator by 5 and the second by 3.

The combined fraction is \(\frac{5\left(4 x + 5\right)-3\left(5 x - 10\right)}{30}\). Open the brackets, collect terms and reduce any common factor.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 11}{6}\).

lessons.title: Multiply and divide algebraic fractions
lessons.summary: Multiply across, use a reciprocal for division and record the original values at which an expression is undefined.
lessons.objective: Multiply across, use a reciprocal for division and record the original values at which an expression is undefined.
lessons.before: For 0580 Extended. Recall how to multiply, divide, add and subtract ordinary fractions. Use brackets to keep a whole numerator or denominator together.
lessons.ideas:
Multiply the top expressions to make one numerator. Multiply the bottom expressions to make one denominator.

The second fraction is the amount you divide by. The reciprocal interchanges its top and bottom.

The two fractions must both be defined. The second fraction must also be non-zero because it is the divisor.
lessons.method:
What do I multiply first?

Cancel any factor that is common to the whole new numerator and denominator. You can also cancel that factor before multiplying when you can see it clearly.

Which fraction do I turn over?

Keep the first fraction and change division into multiplication by the second fraction's reciprocal. For instance, \(\frac{2}{7}\div\frac{3}{5}=\frac{2}{7}\times\frac{5}{3}\).

Which values must be excluded before dividing?

Find zeros of both original denominators. Also find the zeros of the divisor's numerator. With \(\frac{x-4}{x+6}\) as a divisor, exclude \(-6\) and \(4\).
mistakes: Multiplication lets you cancel common factors across the two fractions. In addition, you must combine over a common denominator first.
Only the divisor is inverted. Turning over the first fraction changes the problem.
Flipping the divisor can hide an old denominator. Record its exclusions before taking the reciprocal.

examples.title: Multiply and cancel common factors
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{6 x^{2}}{8}\times\frac{3}{7 x}\) fully.
examples.solution:
Put \(18 x^{2}\) above \(56 x\). The original denominator was non-zero, so \(x\ne 0\).

Cancel one factor of x and reduce the numerical factors of the top and bottom.

The simplified result is \(\frac{9 x}{28}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0\).

examples.title: Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{x + 4}{4 x}\div\frac{x + 10}{8 x}\) fully.
examples.solution:
The second fraction is the divisor. Invert it to write the expression as \(\frac{x + 4}{4 x}\times\frac{8 x}{x + 10}\).

The top and bottom now have a factor of \(x\). Cancel this factor and preserve the exclusions from the original division.

The simplified result is \(\frac{2 x + 8}{x + 10}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0,\quad x\ne -10\).

examples.title: Find where a division is undefined
examples.question: Give every excluded value of \(x\) in \(\frac{1}{x + 6}\div\frac{x - 14}{x + 13}\). List the values.
examples.solution:
The original denominators require \(x\ne -6,\quad x\ne -13\).

The divisor itself must be non-zero. As long as its denominator is non-zero, it is zero at \(x=14\).

The excluded values are \(-13,\;-6,\;14\).

lessons.title: Combine fractions with algebraic denominators
lessons.summary: Choose a common denominator with linear factors, combine numerators and simplify if a factor cancels.
lessons.objective: Choose a common denominator with linear factors, combine numerators and simplify if a factor cancels.
lessons.before: For 0580 Extended. Recall how to multiply, divide, add and subtract ordinary fractions. Use brackets to keep a whole numerator or denominator together.
lessons.ideas:
Look at the factors underneath the fraction bars. The new denominator needs to contain each factor from both old denominators.

Denominators can share a bracket. Use the largest power of each factor needed by either original denominator.

Collect the numerator over the common denominator, then try factorising it. A matching factor may cancel after this step.
lessons.method:
How do I combine two different denominator factors?

For \(x+2\) and \(x-5\), use \((x+2)(x-5)\). Multiply each numerator by the factor missing from its denominator.

When can I reuse a shared factor?

For \(4(x-3)\) and \(6(x-3)\), use \(12(x-3)\). The numbers 4 and 6 both divide 12, and one copy of the bracket is enough.

When can the combined fraction simplify further?

Check the original denominator zeros before cancellation. They are still excluded even if the new formula shows fewer denominator factors.
mistakes: Write the new numerator with brackets before multiplying or subtracting. A minus applies to the whole second product.
Multiplying the denominators always gives a common multiple. A smaller denominator often avoids a factor you would later need to cancel.
An apparent matching term is not enough. Only a common factor of the two whole expressions can be cancelled.

examples.title: Add over two linear factors
examples.question: Write \(\frac{4}{x + 4}+\frac{5}{x + 5}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution:
The two different denominator factors give the common denominator \(\left(x + 4\right) \left(x + 5\right)\).

The new numerator is \(\left(4\right)\left(x + 5\right)+5\left(x + 4\right)\). Expand it and collect like terms.

The simplified result is \(\frac{9 x + 40}{\left(x + 4\right) \left(x + 5\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -4,\quad x\ne -5\).

examples.title: Use a shared algebraic factor once
examples.question: Write \(\frac{13}{6 x + 60}+\frac{6}{8 x + 80}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution:
Both denominators have a factor of \(x + 10\). A lowest common denominator is \(24 \left(x + 10\right)\).

Multiply the first numerator by 4 and the second by 3. The combined numerator is \(70\).

The simplified result is \(\frac{35}{12 \left(x + 10\right)}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -10\).

examples.title: Check for cancellation after combining
examples.question: Write \(\frac{x + 11}{x + 8}-\frac{15}{\left(x + 8\right) \left(x + 13\right)}\) as a single fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution:
Use the denominator \(\left(x + 8\right) \left(x + 13\right)\). Multiply the first numerator by \(x + 13\).

The combined numerator \(x^{2} + 24 x + 128\) factorises as \(\left(x + 8\right) \left(x + 16\right)\). Cancel only the matching factor.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 16}{x + 13}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne -8,\quad x\ne -13\).

lessons.title: Simplify rational expressions and keep restrictions
lessons.summary: Factorise polynomial numerators and denominators, cancel common factors and state the original restrictions.
lessons.objective: Factorise polynomial numerators and denominators, cancel common factors and state the original restrictions.
lessons.before: For 0580 Extended. Recall how to multiply, divide, add and subtract ordinary fractions. Use brackets to keep a whole numerator or denominator together.
lessons.ideas:
First turn the whole numerator and denominator into products. A term within a sum is not automatically a factor of the sum.

Factorise each quadratic separately. A difference of two squares can give two linear factors without trial and error.

A zero in the original denominator makes the original fraction undefined. Simplification gives an equivalent value only where the original expression works.
lessons.method:
Which parts can I cancel?

If every term contains \(x\), take it out first. For instance, \(3x^2+21x=3x(x+7)\). Then look for the same factor below the bar.

What if the numerator and denominator are quadratics?

Use \(A^2-B^2=(A-B)(A+B)\). Compare complete brackets from the top and bottom before cancelling one.

Why do some restrictions survive cancellation?

If a cancelled factor is \(x-9\), the original restriction \(x\ne 9\) remains even when the new formula has no such factor in its denominator.
mistakes: If a term does not contain x, you cannot take out x from the whole expression. Test by multiplying your factors back out.
Brackets such as x + 7 and x − 7 have different zeros. Check the signs as well as the numbers.
When asked for allowed inputs, check every factor of the original denominator. A simplified expression cannot restore an excluded value.

examples.title: Take out a common factor x
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{5 x^{2} + 30 x}{x^{2} + 10 x}\) fully.
examples.solution:
The numerator is \(5 x \left(x + 6\right)\) and the denominator is \(x \left(x + 10\right)\).

Cancel one common factor of \(x\). Preserve the two exclusions from the original denominator.

The simplified result is \(\frac{5 x + 30}{x + 10}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 0,\quad x\ne -10\).

examples.title: Use a difference of squares
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} - 64}{x^{2} + 7 x - 120}\) fully.
examples.solution:
Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 8\right) \left(x + 8\right)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 8\right) \left(x + 15\right)\).

The common factor is \(x - 8\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.

The simplified result is \(\frac{x + 8}{x + 15}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x\ne 8,\quad x\ne -15\).

examples.title: Preserve the original domain after cancelling
examples.question: A student rewrites \(\frac{x^{2} + 6 x - 160}{x^{2} + 8 x - 180}\) as \(\frac{x + 16}{x + 18}\). State the allowed real values of \(x\) for the original expression. Give the restrictions as inequalities or intervals.
examples.solution:
Factorise the original denominator. It is \(\left(x - 10\right) \left(x + 18\right)\), so it is zero at \(-18\) and \(10\).

Keep both exclusions after cancelling. The allowed values meet \(x\ne -18,\quad x\ne 10\).

questions.title: Keep restrictions during cancellation
questions.prompt_html:
1. Simplify \(\frac{x^{2} - 25}{x^{2} + 8 x - 65}\) fully.

    [2]

  2. A student rewrites \(\frac{x^{2} + 4 x - 140}{x^{2} + 8 x - 180}\) as \(\frac{x + 14}{x + 18}\). State the allowed real values of \(x\) for the original expression. Give the restrictions as inequalities or intervals.

    [2]

  3. Simplify \(\frac{10 x^{2} + 60 x}{x^{2} + 11 x}\) fully.

    [2]
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Find factors of both whole polynomials first. Matching terms in a sum cannot cancel by themselves.

(b)

Find the zeros of the starting denominator. A cancelled zero is still excluded.

(c)

Look for a factor of x in every numerator term and every denominator term.
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Factorise the numerator as \(\left(x - 5 ight) \left(x + 5 ight)\) and the denominator as \(\left(x - 5 ight) \left(x + 13 ight)\).

The common factor is \(x - 5\). Cancel it where it is non-zero.

The simplified result is \( rac{x + 5}{x + 13}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x e 5,\quad x e -13\).

(b)

Factorise the original denominator. It is \(\left(x - 10 ight) \left(x + 18 ight)\), so it is zero at \(-18\) and \(10\).

Keep both exclusions after cancelling. The allowed values meet \(x e -18,\quad x e 10\).

(c)

The numerator is \(10 x \left(x + 6 ight)\) and the denominator is \(x \left(x + 11 ight)\).

Cancel one common factor of \(x\). Preserve the two exclusions from the original denominator.

The simplified result is \( rac{10 x + 60}{x + 11}\).

The original restrictions remain \(x e 0,\quad x e -11\).
